Expanding Sourcing Channels

Pre-ordering and Stock Management
Pre-order essential stock of long-lead-time components/raw materials. Ensure ready availability of critical items.
Advance procurements:
Anticipate definitive customer orders and engage in advance procurements. Complete pre- purchase order activities beforehand to streamline procurement and minimise delays.

nodes.title: Measures (intro)
nodes.summary: BEL addresses continuous technology upgrades via a 3-tier R&D structure: Central Research Laboratories for blue-sky and applied research in core technologies; a Product Development and Innovation Centre with Centres of Excellence for engineering modules into products; and Development & Engineering divisions at SBUs for customer requirements and product development. Software SBU and Software Development Centres handle software modules. Challenges are further addressed through planned R&D, systems engineering, training, obsolescence management, and collaborations. To avoid proprietary lock-in, BEL develops modules using alternate technologies and standard protocols with modular, plug-and-play designs and multiple sourcing. Miniaturized platforms address SWaP needs, and obsolescence management includes indigenization.

nodes.summary: This annexure to the Independent Auditors' Report covers: maintenance of proper records for property, plant, equipment, right-of-use assets, and intangible assets; physical verification of PP&E in a phased manner; title deeds of immovable properties not held in the Company's name, with details of gross carrying value, period held, and reasons; use of cost model for PP&E and intangibles; no benami property proceedings; physical verification of inventory and reconciliation; working capital limits and quarterly return filings; investments in associate companies and others; loans to employees and compliance with Sections 185/186; no public deposits accepted and status of old deposits; cost records maintained; statutory dues deposits and outstanding property tax demand; disputed statutory dues across various acts with amounts and forums; no unrecorded income surrendered; no loans/borrowings, no wilful defaulter status; no funds raised via IPO or preferential allotment; no fraud reported; internal audit system; related party compliance; no non-cash transactions with directors; not required to register under RBI; no cash losses; no auditor resignation; no material uncertainty about going concern; CSR unspent amount transferred to special account.

nodes.title: "Annexure B" to the Independent Auditors’ Report
nodes.summary: Annexure B to the Independent Auditors' Report covers the audit of internal financial controls (IFC) over standalone financial statements of Bharat Electronics Limited as of 31 March 2025. It outlines management's responsibility for establishing and maintaining IFC, including design, implementation, and maintenance for orderly business conduct, asset safeguarding, fraud prevention, accurate accounting, and timely financial reporting. It details the auditor's responsibility to express an opinion based on audit procedures, including understanding IFC, risk assessment, and testing design and operating effectiveness. It defines IFC, notes inherent limitations such as collusion and management override, and expresses an unmodified opinion that IFC were adequate and operating effectively. It references reliance on branch auditors' reports for six branches and includes the auditor's signature and date.

nodes.title: "Annexure C" to the Independent Auditors’ Report
nodes.summary: The text includes Annexure C to the Independent Auditors' Report, addressing directions from the Comptroller & Auditor General under Section 143(5) of the Companies Act, 2013 for the year ended 31 March 2025. It covers three audit queries: whether accounting transactions are processed through an IT system (confirmed yes with no implications), whether there is any loan restructuring or waiver due to inability to repay (not applicable as no loans from banks/financial institutions), and whether government grants/subsidies were properly accounted for (no specific scheme funds received; earlier funds properly utilized). The report concludes with auditor signatures. Additionally, the text contains a standalone balance sheet as at 31 March 2025 and 31 March 2024, listing assets (non-current and current) and equity/liabilities (non-current and current) with note references and monetary amounts in lakhs, along with accompanying notes and signatures of the Chairman & Managing Director, Director (Finance) & CFO, Company Secretary, and auditors.

nodes.title: Standalone Balance Sheet
nodes.summary: The text presents the Standalone Balance Sheet as at 31 March 2025 and 31 March 2024, detailing assets (non-current and current) and equity/liabilities (non-current and current). It includes the Standalone Statement of Profit and Loss for the years ended 31 March 2025 and 2024, covering income, expenses, profit, tax, comprehensive income, and earnings per share. It also includes the Standalone Statement of Changes in Equity, showing movements in equity share capital and other equity components. The document concludes with auditor signatures and notes as integral parts of the financial statements.

nodes.title: Standalone Statement of Profit and Loss
nodes.summary: The text presents the Standalone Statement of Profit and Loss, Standalone Statement of Changes in Equity, and Standalone Statement of Cash Flows from the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25. It includes comparative financial data for the years ended 31 March 2025 and 31 March 2024, covering revenue, expenses, profit, tax, comprehensive income, and earnings per share. The Statement of Changes in Equity details movements in equity share capital and other equity reserves. The Statement of Cash Flows summarizes cash flows from operating, investing, and financing activities. The document concludes with signatures of the auditors and company officials.

nodes.title: Standalone Statement of Changes in Equity
nodes.summary: The section presents the Standalone Statement of Changes in Equity for the year ended 31 March 2025, detailing reserves and surplus movements, followed by the Standalone Statement of Cash Flows for 2025 and 2024. It includes comprehensive notes on Property, Plant and Equipment, Capital Work-in-Progress, rental income, intangible assets, investments, trade receivables, loans, deferred tax, inventories, other assets, cash equivalents, equity share capital, reserves, deferred income from government grants, borrowings, trade payables with MSMED disclosures, other financial liabilities, provisions, post-employment benefits, revenue, expenses, related party transactions, and general notes covering EPS, leases, segments, CSR, ratios, fair value, risk management, and recent accounting pronouncements.

nodes.title: Standalone Statement of Changes in Equity (intro)
nodes.summary: The text presents the Standalone Statement of Changes in Equity for the year ended 31 March 2025, showing reserves and surplus movements including profit, transfers, dividends, and share transactions. It then details the Standalone Statement of Cash Flows for 2025 and 2024, covering operating, investing, and financing activities with adjustments and working capital changes. Finally, it includes Standalone Notes to Accounts on Property, Plant and Equipment (gross block, depreciation, additions, land details, useful lives, impairment, and legal issues) and Capital Work-in-Progress (project progress, completion schedules, and impairments).

nodes.title: a. Rental Income
nodes.summary: This section covers rental income and direct operating expenses from investment properties, including depreciation, fair value, deemed cost, useful life, related party transactions, reclassification, and freehold land details. It also includes notes on other intangible assets (software, ERP, development costs) with amortization and deemed cost; intangible assets under development with aging and completion schedules; investments including fair valuation, subsidiaries, associates, and defence organization contributions; trade receivables with aging, provisions, and payment terms; loans with non-current and current categories; other financial assets such as deposits and advances; deferred tax assets and liabilities with reconciliations; inventories with detailed categories and provisions; other assets including advances, contract assets, and prepaid expenses; and cash & cash equivalents, bank balances, current tax, equity share capital, and reserves.

nodes.title: a. Rental Income (intro)
nodes.summary: The text covers rental income and direct operating expenses from properties generating rental income and other properties, depreciation, and profit from investment property, with a note on contractual commitments. It details the fair value of investment properties (land and building) as of March 31, 2025, and 2024, and discusses deemed cost on transition to Ind AS. It outlines the estimation of useful life of assets (buildings: 40 years), depreciation method (straight-line), and related party transactions involving a subsidiary. It also includes details on registration and pending litigation (nil), restrictions on realisability (none), a reclassification of a building from investment property to PP&E, fair value estimation based on government guidance value, and freehold land area in Bengaluru.

nodes.title: Note 4 - Other intangible assets
nodes.summary: Note 4 details other intangible assets, including gross carrying amounts for software licenses/implementation, ERP, and development costs (including funding to development agencies), with additions and deductions for 2024-25 and 2023-24. It presents net carrying amounts and amortisation, showing opening balances, amortisation for the year, deductions, and closing balances. The note also covers deemed cost on transition to Ind AS, estimated useful lives (3 years for software/ERP, 3-15 years for development costs), amortisation on a straight-line basis recognized in profit and loss, the accounting policy reference, contractual commitments (Note 30(6)), impairment (Note 30(4)), and title restrictions governed by agreement terms.

nodes.title: Note 5 - Intangible assets under development
nodes.summary: Note 5 covers intangible assets under development for FY 2024-25 and 2023-24, showing gross block, impairment provision, and net carrying amounts. It includes aging analysis (less than 1 year to more than 3 years) for projects in progress and temporarily suspended. Completion schedules detail time/cost overruns for projects like QRSAM ATULYA, DJAG System, Hemo Dialysis Machine, and others, with expected completion timelines. Suspended projects are listed separately. Impairment disclosures note nil provision current year vs. prior year, write-offs, and amounts charged to profit and loss. Contractual commitments are referenced to Note 30(6).

nodes.title: Note 6 - Investments
nodes.summary: Note 6 details the company's investments, including fair valuation of a loan to a subsidiary (deemed investment). It lists equity instruments in unquoted subsidiaries, associates, and others, measured at amortized cost or FVOCI, with share counts and values. Other investments include co-operative societies at amortized cost and LIC at FVTPL. It provides aggregate investment values and impairment, references financial instrument classification (Note 32), and explains contributions to Defence Innovation Organisation, BEL IAI Aerosystems, and various defence testing foundations (EWDTF, CDTF, UASTF, LENS), along with LIC leave encashment investment. It also covers FVOCI strategic investments, dividend income, and related party disclosure reference (Note 31).

nodes.title: Note 7 - Trade receivables
nodes.summary: Note 7 presents trade receivables for March 2025 and March 2024, split into non-current and current, secured/unsecured and doubtful, with provisions including liquidated damages. Detailed aging tables classify billed and unbilled receivables by undisputed/disputed status and periods from due date. Payment terms cover delivery-based dues, retention linked to installation or milestones, contract liabilities from advances, and contract assets. It also references financial instruments, impairment policy, related party disclosures, and security/hypothecation.

nodes.title: Note 8 - Loans
nodes.summary: Note 8 - Loans presents the company's loan balances as at 31 March 2025 and 31 March 2024, split into non-current and current categories. Non-current loans include unsecured, considered good loans to employees and unsecured, considered doubtful others, with provisions reducing the latter to nil; sub-total (A) is 663 and 703. Current loans include unsecured, considered good loans to related parties, others, and employees, with sub-total (B) of 147 and 810, giving total (A+B) of 810 and 844. The note also includes a footnote on credit-impaired loans of 132, and cross-references financial instruments (Note 32), impairment of financial assets per Accounting Policy No. 30, related party disclosure (Note 31), and security/hypothecation (Note 34).

nodes.title: Note 9 - Other financial assets
nodes.summary: Note 9 - Other financial assets presents non-current and current other financial assets as at 31 March 2025 and 31 March 2024, including security deposits, bank deposits with over 12 months maturity (margin money for bank guarantees), advances to employees and others, receivables other than trade receivables, interest accrued on term deposits, and other assets, with provisions for doubtful amounts. It references Note 32 for financial instrument classification, states that impairment provisions follow Accounting Policy No. 30, refers to Note 31 for related party disclosures, notes that Nil net carrying amount of property, plant and equipment not in active use and pending disposal is included in other assets, and refers to Note 34 for security and hypothecation details.

nodes.title: Note 10 - Deferred tax assets (net)
nodes.summary: The note presents deferred tax assets and liabilities as of March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, detailing income tax recognized in profit or loss, other comprehensive income, and directly in equity. It includes a reconciliation of effective tax rates, a breakdown of deferred tax assets and liabilities by nature, and movements for the years ended March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024. It also states that there are no tax losses carried forward with recognized deferred tax assets and no unrecognized deferred tax assets or liabilities.

nodes.title: Note 11 - Inventories
nodes.summary: Note 11 - Inventories presents a detailed breakdown of inventory categories (raw materials, work in progress, finished goods, stores and spares, loose tools, stock in trade, disposal scrap) for current and non-current portions as at March 31, 2025 and 2024, including provisions and in-transit adjustments. It includes notes on materials with sub-contractors, stock verification discrepancies and related provisions, valuation policy, carbon credits (CERs) held as finished goods, depreciation and operation costs of emission reduction equipment, security/hypothecation reference, write-down and reversal of inventory write-downs recognized in profit and loss, impairment provisions, materials located at customer premises, and customer-owned assets retained under contractual terms.

nodes.title: Note 12 - Other assets
nodes.summary: Note 12 - Other assets presents a comparative table of non-current and current assets as at 31 March 2025 and 31 March 2024, including capital advances, advances for purchases with provisions, contract assets with provisions, balances with government authorities, prepaid expenses, prepaid taxes, claims receivable, contract costs, advances to employees, and other assets, with subtotals and total. It also covers impairment of non-financial assets per accounting policy, related party disclosure reference, closing balances of contract costs, amortisation and impairment of contract costs, impairment of contract assets, and a reference to security and hypothecation in Note 34.

nodes.title: Note 13 - Cash & cash equivalents
nodes.summary: Note 13 covers cash and cash equivalents as of March 31, 2025, and March 31, 2024, including balance with banks, cash on hand, and term deposits, with references to financial instrument classification, repatriation restrictions, maturity-based classification, and security/hypothecation. Note 14 details bank balances other than cash and cash equivalents, including term deposits and unpaid dividend account, with similar references. Note 15 presents current tax assets and liabilities. Note 16a covers equity share capital, including authorized and issued capital, reconciliation of shares outstanding, shareholders holding over 5%, bonus shares, buybacks, reserves, terms and rights of shares, and dividends. Note 16b describes the nature and purpose of reserves, specifically capital reserve.

nodes.title: Standalone Trade Payables and Borrowings Notes

nodes.title: Current Trade Payable 2023-24
nodes.summary: The section on Current Trade Payable 2023-24 covers Notes 20–31 to the standalone financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2025. It includes other financial liabilities, provisions, post-employment benefits (gratuity, BERECHS, provident fund, compensated absences, pension), other liabilities, revenue, other income, inventory changes, employee benefits, finance costs, depreciation, other expenses, related party transactions, and general notes (EPS, compliance, borrowings, commitments, contingencies, leases, segments, CSR, ratios). Specific items include interest reversed during the year, MSMED Act disclosures, loans to related parties (e.g., BELOP term loan), management contracts and deputation of BEL employees, exemptions for government-related entities under Ind AS 24, investments and fair valuation of a loan to BELOP, incorporation details of Defence Innovation Organisation, BEL IAI Aerosystems, and defence testing foundations, fair value measurements, risk management framework, capital management, pledged assets, critical accounting estimates, and recent accounting pronouncements.

nodes.title: c. The interest reversed by the company during the year ended 31 March
nodes.summary: This section encompasses Notes 20 through 31 to the standalone financial statements for the year ended 31 March 2025. It covers other financial liabilities, provisions and post-employment benefits (gratuity, BERECHS, provident fund, compensated absences, pension), other liabilities, revenue from operations, other income, changes in inventories, employee benefits expense, finance costs, depreciation and amortisation, other expenses, related party transactions, and general notes. The general notes address earnings per share, compliance, borrowing details, commitments, contingencies, leases, segment reporting, CSR, financial ratios, and other disclosures. nodes.title: c. The interest reversed by the company during the year ended 31 March (intro)
nodes.summary: The text presents a detailed breakdown of current trade payables for 2023-24, categorizing MSME and other dues, including disputed amounts and unbilled/billed but not due items. It provides an aging analysis of outstanding amounts by due date (less than 1 year to over 3 years) and includes a separate aging schedule for MSME dues. It also discloses information required under the MSMED Act, 2006 for 2024-25 and 2023-24, covering unpaid principal and interest, interest paid, reversed, accrued, and payable, with a note on inclusion under Note 20. The text further references financial instruments (Note 32), related party disclosures (Note 31), and currency/liquidity risk exposure (Note 33), and notes that MSME identification is based on available information.

nodes.title: Note 20 - Other financial liabilities
nodes.summary: Note 20 presents other financial liabilities as at 31 March 2025 and 31 March 2024, split into non-current and current subtotals. Non-current includes security deposits including retention money. Current items include security deposits, interest accrued on trade payables, non-trade payables, unpaid matured deposits, unpaid dividend, dues to micro and small enterprises, outstanding expenses, and other liabilities. It provides total liabilities and the amount to be transferred to the Investor Education & Protection Fund (Nil). Footnotes reference Note 19, capital items payable, and unspent CSR expenditure provision. It also refers to Note 32 for financial instrument classification and includes page references.

nodes.title: Note 21 - Provisions
nodes.summary: Note 21 covers provisions and post-employment benefits. It presents the movement of provisions for 2024-25 and 2023-24 for employee benefits (long-term compensated absences, provident fund interest, gratuity, BERECHS) and others (onerous contracts, performance warranty, site restoration), including opening balances, additions, utilizations, reversals, and closing balances. Accounting policies and measurement bases are outlined for warranties, site restoration, and onerous contracts. Detailed disclosures cover the funded gratuity plan (obligations, plan assets, expenses, remeasurements, balance sheet recognition, assumptions, sensitivity, maturity profile), BERECHS (funded health scheme, obligations, assets, expenses, assumptions, sensitivity, maturity), and provident fund interest shortfall (obligations, assets, expenses, assumptions). Long-term compensated absences (non-funded scheme, expenses, liabilities, assumptions) and the pension scheme (defined contribution and defined benefit risks, asset-liability matching, funding policy) are also described.

nodes.summary: The text covers standalone notes to accounts for FY 2024-25, detailing provisions for warranties (based on SBU-level trend estimates at present value), site restoration (lease obligation at present value of best estimate), onerous contracts (expected losses at present value), and performance warranty obligations where vendor back-to-back warranties exist. nodes.title: (ii) BEL RETIRED EMPLOYEES CONTRIBUTORY HEALTH SCHEME (BERECHS) :
nodes.summary: The text details BEL Retired Employees' Contributory Health Scheme (BERECHS), a funded contributory health scheme for retired employees and spouses, with the company remitting shortfall to BREM Trust based on actuarial valuation. It summarizes net benefit expense, balance sheet recognition, and changes in present value of obligations (including service cost, interest cost, benefits paid, actuarial gains/losses from financial, experience, and demographic assumptions). It covers changes in fair value of plan assets, expenses recognized in profit & loss, remeasurements in OCI, balance sheet amounts (funded status, asset ceiling), and plan asset categories (99.99% insurer-managed funds, 0.01% bank balance). Actuarial assumptions (discount rate, medical inflation, attrition), best estimate of contributions, sensitivity analysis for healthcare cost trends and discount/medical inflation rate movements, and maturity profile of defined benefit obligation are also included.

nodes.title: (iii) EMPLOYEES PROVIDENT FUND [INTEREST SHORTFALL] :
nodes.summary: The text details the Employees Provident Fund interest shortfall, managed by the Company's Provident Fund Trust. It covers the recognition of contributions and interest shortfalls as expenses, actuarial valuation assumptions, and changes in present value of benefit obligations and fair value of plan assets for 2024-25 and 2023-24. It includes expenses recognized in profit and loss, amounts in the balance sheet, experience adjustments, and remeasurements in other comprehensive income. Asset categories and actuarial assumptions like discount rate and salary escalation are provided, along with notes on interest shortfall and non-performing investments recoverable from the enterprise.

nodes.title: B. Long Term Compensated Absence :
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Company's non-funded Long Term Compensated Absence Scheme, detailing leave types for executives (Annual and Half Pay Leave) and non-executives (Annual and Sick Leave), and compensation upon superannuation, VRS, death, or resignation, with AL encashable during service. It presents a table summarizing net benefit expenses in the Statement of Profit & Loss and balance sheet liabilities for 2024-25 and 2023-24, including expense breakdowns for leave encashed and provisions, actuarial assumptions (discount rate and compensation increase rate), and expected settlement of leave obligations within and beyond 12 months.

nodes.title: C. Pension Scheme :
nodes.summary: The text covers the company's defined contribution pension scheme and defined benefit plans (Gratuity and BERECHS). It describes specific risks for defined benefit plans, including movements in long-term government bond rates affecting discount rates and present value of obligations, and salary escalation/benefit risks versus actual experience, both mitigated by annual valuations. It outlines asset-liability matching strategies, noting limited flexibility due to predominantly insurer-managed funds. Finally, it details funding arrangements and policy for the Gratuity and BERECHS Medical plans, both funded with 99.99% insurer-managed assets, and annual contributions set equal to the deficit from preceding actuarial valuations.

It then details Note 33 on financial instruments, including accounting classification and fair values of financial assets and liabilities (measured at FVPL, FVOCI, and amortised cost), fair value hierarchy levels (1, 2, 3), and valuation techniques, particularly for LIC investments. nodes.summary: The page presents Note 33 on financial instruments fair value measurements, split into two sections. Section 1 covers accounting classification and fair values, showing carrying amounts and fair values of financial assets (measured at FVPL, FVOCI, or amortised cost) and financial liabilities (measured at fair value or not), with separate tables for 31 March 2025 and 2024. Assets include investments, trade receivables, loans, cash, bank balances, and other financial assets; liabilities include borrowings, trade payables, and other financial liabilities. Section 2 details the fair value hierarchy (Levels 1, 2, and 3) for recurring measurements, listing financial assets at FVPL and FVOCI, and notes that amortised cost assets and liabilities have carrying values approximating fair value. Level definitions are provided.

Market risk (foreign exchange and interest rate) is discussed, with currency risk exposures in USD, Euro, GBP, CHF, and Yen, sensitivity analysis, and hedging policies (up to 50% hedging, forward contracts, no outstanding forwards as of March 2025). Interest rate risk includes variable rate borrowings for the parent company and subsidiary BELOP, with sanctioned limits and outstanding balances.

nodes.title: Financial Risk Management: Framework, Market, Currency and Interest Rate Risks
key_items: Note 34 - Financial risk management i. Risk Management framework and policies
nodes.summary: The page covers Note 34 on financial risk management. It begins with a fair valuation note for an unlisted investment (Mana Effluent Treatment Plant Ltd) using the Net Asset Value method. It then outlines the Risk Management framework and policies, including Board and Risk Management Committee responsibilities, a centralized Treasury function, hedging practices, and a no-speculation policy. Market risk is defined, followed by detailed currency risk exposure across USD, Euro, GBP, CHF, and JPY, including forward contract status, foreign currency sensitivity analysis, and interest rate risk (fair value and cash flow risks).

nodes.title: Variable Rate Borrowing:
nodes.summary: The text covers variable rate borrowing details for the parent company and subsidiary BELOP, including sanctioned limits, utilization, interest rates, and outstanding balances. It discusses equity price risk as negligible and details liquidity risk management, including contractual maturity analysis of financial liabilities for 2025 and 2024. Credit risk management is described, covering trade receivables, bank deposits, and other financial assets. Finally, capital management objectives, bonus shares, dividend policy, borrowing limits, and gearing ratio are presented.

nodes.title: Consolidated Notes: Equity Price, Liquidity, and Credit Risk Disclosures
nodes.summary: This page presents three consolidated notes: Equity Price Risk (negligible due to minimal equity investments), Liquidity Risk (minimal, with prudent management, cash flow monitoring, and contractual maturity tables of financial liabilities for 2025 and 2024), and Credit Risk (managed via risk committee, government receivables, letters of credit, bank deposit policies, and negligible other financial asset risk).

nodes.title: x. Capital Management
nodes.summary: The text covers the Group's capital management objectives, including maintaining a strong capital base, conservative debt approach, bonus share issuance in FY 2022-23, dividend distribution policy, and sanctioned borrowing limits. It provides gearing ratio data and details assets pledged as security for working capital borrowings, including a subsidiary's mortgage. It outlines critical accounting estimates and judgments regarding R&D expenditure, defined benefit obligations, warranty provisions, revenue recognition, intangible assets, and leases. Finally, it notes recent accounting pronouncements (Ind AS 117 and amendments to Ind AS 116) with no significant impact.

nodes.summary: The text covers recent accounting pronouncements, including MCA's notification of Ind AS 117 and amendments to Ind AS 116, with no significant impact expected. It then presents material accounting policies for Bharat Electronics Limited's consolidated financial statements: corporate information (a public sector defence electronics company in Bengaluru), basis of preparation (Indian GAAP/Ind AS), use of estimates, basis of measurement (historical cost except fair value items like derivatives and defined benefit assets/liabilities), functional currency (INR), and detailed revenue recognition policies covering performance obligations satisfied over time or at a point in time, including specific contract types (Ex-Works, FOR, Bill and Hold), measurement of transaction price, and allocation for multiple performance obligations including bundled contracts.

nodes.title: Corporate Information and Basis of Preparation of Financial Statements
key_items: Material Accounting Policies 1. Basis of Preparation
nodes.summary: The page covers the corporate information of Bharat Electronics Limited, a public sector enterprise under the Department of Defence Production, Ministry of Defence, domiciled in India and listed on two recognized stock exchanges, manufacturing and supplying electronic equipment and systems to the defence sector with limited civilian presence. It also covers the material accounting policy on the basis of preparation, stating that the financial statements are prepared and presented in accordance with Indian GAAP, comprising mandatory Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) notified under the Companies Act, 2013, and the provisions of the Companies Act, 2013, consistently applied.

nodes.title: 2. Use of Estimates
key_items: A. Revenue from Contract with Customers
nodes.summary: The text covers material accounting policies under Ind AS: use of estimates and recognition of differences; basis of measurement (historical cost except derivatives, qualifying financial instruments, and defined benefit plans at fair value); functional and presentation currency (INR); revenue recognition from contracts with customers (performance obligations satisfied over time or at a point in time, including AMC contracts, Ex-Works, FOR, bill and hold sales, measurement, bundled/multiple element contracts, penalties, significant financing component) and other income (interest, dividend, rental, duty drawbacks, and other income on accrual); property, plant and equipment and capital work-in-progress; intangible assets and intangible assets under development; depreciation/amortisation; disposal of property, plant and equipment; and research and development expenditure.

nodes.title: Accounting Policies for Revenue, PPE, Intangibles, Depreciation and Disposal
key_items: 9. Disposal of Property, Plant and Equipment
nodes.summary: The page details material accounting policies under Ind AS, covering revenue recognition for multiple elements and penalties, treatment of significant financing components, and recognition of other income including interest, dividends, rent and duty drawbacks. It outlines initial and subsequent measurement of property, plant and equipment, capital work-in-progress, and intangible assets including those under development. Depreciation and amortisation policies are described, including straight-line basis, useful lives differing from Schedule II, component accounting, and annual review of residual values and useful lives. Finally, it addresses derecognition and disposal of property, plant and equipment, with gains or losses recognised in profit and loss.

nodes.title: 10. Research and Development Expenditure
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for research and development expenditure, technical know-how, investment property, and impairment of non-financial assets. It details that research costs are expensed when incurred. Development costs are generally expensed, except for specific contracts, joint projects with expected benefits, and NCNC trials, which may be capitalized or carried forward under conditions. Technical know-how is expensed unless it qualifies as an intangible asset. Investment properties are initially at cost, subsequently at cost less depreciation and impairment. Impairment of non-financial assets is assessed at each reporting date, with recoverable amount determined as the higher of fair value less costs of disposal and value in use, and reversals recognized upon increased service potential.

nodes.title: 14. Leases
nodes.summary: The text outlines lease accounting policies under Ind AS 116 for both lessee and lessor. As lessee, it covers recognition of right-of-use assets at present value of lease payments plus initial direct costs, subsequent cost model measurement, depreciation over shorter of useful life or lease term, lease liability presented as borrowing, allocation of payments between liability and finance cost, discounting using implicit rate or incremental borrowing rate, expense treatment for short-term and low-value leases, and accounting for lease modifications. As lessor, it classifies leases as finance or operating, detailing finance lease recognition of net investment as receivable, finance income recognition, impairment testing under Ind AS 109, and operating lease income recognition, along with treatment of lease modifications.

nodes.title: 15. Borrowing Costs
nodes.summary: The text covers material accounting policies: borrowing costs capitalisation and expensing; government grants measured at fair value, deferred income recognition tied to depreciation or expenditure; inventories valued at lower of cost or net realisable value, with disposable scrap at net realisable value and provisions for aged items; income taxes including current tax measurement and deferred tax via balance sheet method; warranty provisions based on trend estimates; foreign currency transaction and translation rules; employee benefits covering short-term, long-term compensated absences, gratuity, provident fund, BERECHS, actuarial recognition, plan changes, voluntary retirement, and defined contribution plans; provisions including recognition, reimbursement, onerous contracts and discounting, plus contingent liabilities/assets disclosure; and cash flow statement preparation under the indirect method.

nodes.title: Ind AS Accounting Policies on Taxes, Forex, Benefits, Provisions
key_items: 18. Income Taxes; 20. Foreign currency transactions and translation
nodes.summary: The page sets out material Ind AS accounting policies covering inventory valuation; income taxes including current and deferred tax recognition and measurement; warranty provisions based on trend or management estimates; foreign currency transaction and translation rules; employee benefits covering short-term, long-term compensated absences, gratuity, provident fund, BERECHS, actuarial recognition in OCI, plan amendments, voluntary retirement, and defined contribution plans; and provisions and contingent liabilities/assets covering recognition, reimbursement, onerous contracts, discounting, and disclosure.

nodes.title: 23. Cash Flow Statement
nodes.summary: The text covers material accounting policies for consolidated financial statements, including: preparation of the cash flow statement using the indirect method per Ind AS 7; fair value measurement with a three-level hierarchy; financial assets covering initial recognition, subsequent measurement categories, derecognition, and trade receivables; forward contracts and embedded derivatives; cash and cash equivalents; impairment of financial assets using the expected credit loss model; financial liabilities including initial recognition, subsequent measurement, loans and borrowings, and trade payables; reclassification of financial instruments; offsetting of financial instruments; cash and non-cash distributions to equity holders; and errors and estimates with retrospective or prospective application.

nodes.title: Material Accounting Policies for Financial Instruments and Equity Distributions
key_items: 33. Cash Dividend and Non-Cash distribution to Equity Holders
nodes.summary: This page outlines key accounting policies: fair value measurement with hierarchy levels; financial assets' initial recognition, subsequent measurement categories, derecognition, and receivables; forward contracts and embedded derivatives; cash and cash equivalents definition; impairment using expected credit loss model with specific considerations for government dues, disputed amounts, and aged receivables; financial liabilities' initial and subsequent measurement, including loans, borrowings, payables, and fair value through profit or loss; reclassification rules for financial instruments; offsetting criteria; and recognition of liabilities for cash and non-cash distributions to equity holders.

nodes.title: 34. Errors and Estimates
nodes.summary: The text covers accounting policies for errors and estimates: retrospective application for policy changes and material error corrections, prospective application for estimate changes. It details earnings per share calculations (basic and diluted) and events after the reporting period (adjusting vs. non-adjusting). Consolidation principles are outlined, including line-by-line combination, equity method for associates, recognition of goodwill or capital reserve, and uniform accounting policies. The document includes signatures of auditors and directors, and a Form AOC-I listing subsidiary details such as names (BEL Thales, BEL Optronic Devices Limited), financial figures (share capital, reserves, assets, liabilities, investments, turnover, profits, dividends, shareholding percentages), and notes on subsidiaries yet to commence operations or liquidated/sold during the year.

nodes.title: Accounting Policies: EPS, Subsequent Events, Consolidation Principles
nodes.summary: The page from the Integrated Annual Report 2024-25 covers material accounting policies for consolidated financial statements. It addresses retrospective revision for material errors, restating comparatives and opening balances. Section 35 explains basic and diluted earnings per share calculations, including adjustments for own shares and dilutive potential ordinary shares. Section 36 distinguishes adjusting events (adjusted before authorization) from non-adjusting events (disclosed only). Section 37 details consolidation principles: line-by-line combination of holding, subsidiary, and step-down subsidiary financials, elimination of intra-group balances, equity method for associates, treatment of reserves, uniform accounting policies, and recognition of goodwill or capital reserve on consolidation. It concludes with auditor and director signatures.

nodes.summary: The text presents Part A on subsidiaries, listing names (BEL Thales, BEL Optronic Devices Limited, Systems Limited) and financial details such as share capital, reserves, assets, liabilities, investments, turnover, profits, dividends, and shareholding percentages, noting no subsidiaries are yet to commence operations or were liquidated. Part B covers associates and joint ventures, including names, audited balance sheet dates, shares held, investment amounts, holding percentages, significant influence, non-consolidation reasons, net worth, and profit/loss, with no associates yet to commence or liquidated. It concludes with auditor and director signatures and dates.
